title: How far should the pads be?
title_plain: How far should the pads be?
summary: The wait of urgent cargo grows by {{r:standoff_pct}} of distance between the landing pads and the base, but close pads spray the base with ejecta.
summary_plain: The wait of urgent cargo grows by 35.0 % per km of distance between the landing pads and the base, but close pads spray the base with ejecta.
notes: E20 pooled law at the typical fleet load (results/table_E20.csv) and the E20 siting model (results/E20_fit.json). Wording for LEAD to edit.

standoff_pct.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = standoff, column pct_per_unit; pooled fit of ln(urgent mean delay), 100 (e^b - 1) per km of pad standoff, at the typical fleet load (experiment E20)
standoff_pct.label: Urgent wait per km of pad distance

standoff_lo.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = standoff, column ci_lo; as a percentage, 100 (e^v - 1); lower end of the 95 % bootstrap interval over seeds
standoff_lo.label: Lower end of its interval

standoff_hi.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = standoff, column ci_hi; as a percentage, 100 (e^v - 1); upper end of the 95 % bootstrap interval over seeds
standoff_hi.label: Upper end of its interval

fit_years.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = standoff, column n; rows of the pooled fit: one seed of one cell each (E17 + E18)
fit_years.label: Simulated years in the fit

fit_seeds.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = standoff, column n_seeds
fit_seeds.label: Seeds per setting

keepout_pct.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = keepout, column pct_per_unit; per km of plume keep-out radius
keepout_pct.label: Urgent wait per km of keep-out radius

keepout_lo.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = keepout, column ci_lo; as a percentage, 100 (e^v - 1); 95 % bootstrap interval, lower end
keepout_lo.label: Lower end of its interval

keepout_hi.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = keepout, column ci_hi; as a percentage, 100 (e^v - 1); 95 % bootstrap interval, upper end
keepout_hi.label: Upper end of its interval

miss_pct.source: results/table_E20.csv, row response = log_delay_prio1_mean_h, subset = pooled, term = log_miss, column pct_per_unit; per e-fold of the mean landing miss
miss_pct.label: Urgent wait per e-fold of landing miss

impacts_near.source: results/E20_fit.json: siting/impacts_per_landing_at_standoffs/0.5; ejecta impacts on the base per landing at a 0.5 km standoff, Modelled from the Wittal et al. (2022) anchors
impacts_near.label: Ejecta impacts per landing, nearest pads

impacts_far.source: results/E20_fit.json: siting/impacts_per_landing_at_standoffs/5; the same at a 5 km standoff
impacts_far.label: The same, farthest pads

far_cheapest.source: results/E20_fit.json: siting/share_of_minima_by_standoff/13/share_min_at_5km; x 100; share of the fleet and dispatch cells whose cheapest standoff is 5 km, at energy 500 $/kWh, damage 1 M$ per impact, delay valued at 100 $ per item-hour (prices Assumed)
far_cheapest.label: Cells where the farthest pads cost least

steps.title: Every kilometre costs time
steps.text: Rovers carry each delivery from the pads to the base. The mean wait of urgent cargo grows by {{r:standoff_pct}} of standoff, with an interval of {{r:standoff_lo}} to {{r:standoff_hi}}.
steps.visual: The base and its two landing pads, with the rover routes between them drawn on the ground.
steps.text_plain: Rovers carry each delivery from the pads to the base. The mean wait of urgent cargo grows by 35.0 % per km of standoff, with an interval of 32.6 % to 37.6 %.
steps.visual_plain: The base and its two landing pads, with the rover routes between them drawn on the ground.

steps.title: Where the law comes from
steps.text: One fit over {{r:fit_years}} from {{r:fit_seeds}}: every fleet size, job rule, landing accuracy and pad size of the study.
steps.visual: The whole base from above, rovers driving between pads, depot and work sites.
steps.text_plain: One fit over 62,640 simulated years from 30 seeds: every fleet size, job rule, landing accuracy and pad size of the study.
steps.visual_plain: The whole base from above, rovers driving between pads, depot and work sites.

steps.title: Keep-out zones barely matter
steps.text: Clearing a plume keep-out zone during each landing changes the wait by {{r:keepout_pct}} of keep-out radius, an interval of {{r:keepout_lo}} to {{r:keepout_hi}} that includes zero. The fleets are idle most of the time and absorb the evacuations.
steps.visual: A ring around the active pad marks the plume keep-out zone; rovers wait outside it until the lander is down.
steps.text_plain: Clearing a plume keep-out zone during each landing changes the wait by −0.5 % per km of keep-out radius, an interval of −1.5 % to 0.8 % that includes zero. The fleets are idle most of the time and absorb the evacuations.
steps.visual_plain: A ring around the active pad marks the plume keep-out zone; rovers wait outside it until the lander is down.

steps.title: Landing accuracy acts through the pad edge
steps.text: Each e-fold of the mean landing miss adds {{r:miss_pct}}, because landings off the pad mean longer, rougher drives.
steps.visual: Touchdown points scattered around the pad; the ones outside its rim are highlighted.
steps.title_plain: Landing accuracy acts through the pad edge
steps.text_plain: Each e-fold of the mean landing miss adds 8.2 %, because landings off the pad mean longer, rougher drives.
steps.visual_plain: Touchdown points scattered around the pad; the ones outside its rim are highlighted.

steps.title: Close pads spray the base
steps.text: A landing blasts regolith outward. At the nearest standoff studied the model expects about {{r:impacts_near}} ejecta impacts on the base per landing; at the farthest, {{r:impacts_far}}.
steps.visual: The ejecta fan from a landing on the near pad reaching the base buildings.
steps.text_plain: A landing blasts regolith outward. At the nearest standoff studied the model expects about 12 ejecta impacts on the base per landing; at the farthest, 0.37.
steps.visual_plain: The ejecta fan from a landing on the near pad reaching the base buildings.

steps.title: So: far, unless energy is dear
steps.text: Pricing hauling, ejecta damage and waiting time together, the farthest standoff studied is cheapest in {{r:far_cheapest}} of the cells at middle prices. Only cheap damage, together with dear energy or highly valued time, pulls the pads closer.
steps.visual: The base from a distance, with the pads at the far end of their routes.
steps.title_plain: So: far, unless energy is dear
steps.text_plain: Pricing hauling, ejecta damage and waiting time together, the farthest standoff studied is cheapest in 100 % of the cells at middle prices. Only cheap damage, together with dear energy or highly valued time, pulls the pads closer.
steps.visual_plain: The base from a distance, with the pads at the far end of their routes.
